mainTopic: Saving food from a fire on שבת: the three-meal limit and its reason, the broken-barrel ברייתא and הערמה, bread customs learned from the מן, and the number of שבת meals
overview: This amud opens by finishing a discussion from the previous משנה. רב אשי defines a closed alley and an open alley for bringing כתבי הקודש there during a fire, and he explains that even רבי אליעזר agrees one לחי is enough for a ספר תורה. A new משנה then teaches that during a fire on שבת one may save food only for the meals still left, while רבי יוסי says one may always save three meals' worth. רבא explains the limit: a panicked owner might come to put out the fire. אביי challenges this from a ברייתא about a broken barrel on a roof, and רבא answers that the barrel case has its own decree about carrying through רשות הרבים. The גמרא then studies that ברייתא in full, including the rule about guests and a dispute over הערמה. It asks whether that dispute matches the argument of רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע about an animal and its offspring in a pit, and it rejects the comparison. More ברייתות follow about which bread may be saved and about bread left in the oven, which must be removed with a knife to make a change on שבת. Next come teachings learned from the מן: rising early on Friday, לחם משנה, and customs about breaking the שבת bread. Last, the גמרא returns to the משנה, brings the dispute over whether there are three or four שבת meals, and begins checking whose view the משנה follows, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: רב אשי defines a closed alley and an open alley
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי gives a new definition: three walls with one לחי is a closed alley, and three walls with no לחי is an open alley.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב אשי said: three walls and one side-post, that is the closed alley. Three walls without a side-post, that is the open alley.
steps.whatsHappening: Earlier explanations of the previous משנה's terms 'closed alley' and 'open alley' were rejected, so רב אשי now offers his own definitions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word אלא signals that earlier answers failed and a fresh approach is coming. For רב אשי, the difference between the two alleys is not about the alley being open at both ends. It is about whether the fourth side has a לחי. One לחי makes the alley 'closed' enough to carry כתבי הקודש into it, and with no לחי at all it counts as 'open'.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather (rejects the earlier answers and brings a new one)
A side-post at the entrance of an alley that makes carrying there permitted
An alley that opens onto the public domain
Open / passing through (here: lacking a לחי)

steps.confusionAlert: Normally 'מבוי מפולש' means an alley open at both ends. In רב אשי's reading it means an alley with three walls and no לחי at all. Don't bring in the usual meaning here.

phrases.english: Rather, Rav Ashi said:
Three walls and one side-post —
this is the alley that is not open (closed).
Three walls without a side-post —
this is the open alley.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces explanations rejected on the previous daf
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Earlier explanations of 'open' and 'closed' alley were not workable
steps.terutzMaskana: Closed means three walls plus one לחי. Open means three walls with no לחי.

steps.title: Even רבי אליעזר agrees that one post is enough for a ספר תורה
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי adds that even רבי אליעזר, who requires two לחיים, only means this for food and drink. For a ספר תורה, one לחי is enough.
steps.simpleTranslation: And even according to רבי אליעזר, who said we need two side-posts, that applies only to food and drink. But for a ספר תורה, one side-post is enough.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי heads off a challenge: how can one לחי be enough, when רבי אליעזר says an alley needs two? He answers that for a ספר תורה even רבי אליעזר is lenient.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר's demand for two לחיים applies to ordinary carrying of food and drink. Saving a ספר תורה from a fire is treated more leniently, so a single לחי is enough. This way רב אשי's definition works according to every opinion.

keyTerms.meaning: These words apply only to (a limitation)

steps.whatToRemember: According to רב אשי, one לחי is enough to bring a ספר תורה into an alley during a fire, even according to רבי אליעזר.

phrases.english: And even according to Rabbi Eliezer
who said we require two side-posts,
those words apply to food and drinks,
but for a Torah scroll —
one side-post is enough.

steps.triggerLanguage: וַאֲפִילּוּ לְרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר דְּאָמַר בָּעֵינַן לְחָיַיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends רב אשי's definition so it holds even according to רבי אליעזר
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: For a ספר תורה, one לחי is enough according to all opinions.

steps.title: New משנה: how much food may be saved from a fire on שבת
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that one may save food for three meals from a fire on שבת, for people and for animals, and the amount shrinks as שבת goes on.
steps.simpleTranslation: One may save food for three meals. Food fit for a person is saved for a person, and food fit for an animal is saved for an animal. How so? If a fire broke out on Friday night, one saves food for three meals. In the morning, one saves food for two meals. In the afternoon, one saves food for one meal.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It sets a limit on how much food a person may save from a burning house on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One may save only as much as is needed for the remaining שבת meals. There are three שבת meals: Friday night, שבת morning, and the afternoon. So the amount depends on how many meals are still left when the fire starts. The same rule applies to animal food for one's animals.

keyTerms.meaning: How so? (introduces the explanation of a rule)

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the basis for the halacha that one may save only what is needed for the rest of שבת, and the rest of the sugya asks why such a limit exists.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
One may rescue food for three meals.
What is fit for a person — for a person,
what is fit for an animal — for an animal.
How so?
If a fire broke out on Friday night —
one may rescue food for three meals.
In the morning — one may rescue food for two meals.
In the afternoon — food for one meal.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: New משנה; new topic
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One may save food only for the שבת meals that remain: three on Friday night, two in the morning, one in the afternoon.

steps.title: רבי יוסי: always three meals
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי disagrees and says one may always save food for three meals, whatever the time of day.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי says: one may always save food for three meals.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה brings a dissenting opinion. רבי יוסי does not shrink the amount as שבת goes on.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יוסי, 'three meals' is a fixed amount the חכמים permitted. It is not calculated by how many meals are left. So even in the afternoon, one may save food for three meals.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei says:
One may always rescue food for three meals.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with the first view of the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Three meals' worth may always be saved, at any time on שבת.

steps.title: Why limit saving permitted food at all?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: since the person is only moving permitted food, why not let him save more?
steps.simpleTranslation: Now, since he is going to the trouble with something permitted, let him save more!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the משנה's limit. Moving food within a permitted area is not a מלאכה, so why stop at three meals?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The assumption is that the saving is being done in a permitted way, such as into a courtyard with an עירוב. If nothing forbidden is being done, there seems to be no reason for a limit. The גמרא wants to know what the limit is protecting against.

phrases.english: GEMARA:
Now, since he is exerting himself with something permitted,
let him rescue more?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the reason behind the משנה's limit
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Moving permitted items in a permitted area involves no prohibition, so a limit seems pointless.

steps.title: רבא: a panicked person might put out the fire
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains that a person panics about his property, so if he is allowed to save everything he may end up extinguishing the fire.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: since a person is panicked about his money, if you allow him, he will come to put out the fire.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the question. The limit is a גזירה, a protective rabbinic decree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the person were allowed to save everything, he would stay busy and frantic around the fire, and in that state he might forget it is שבת and put it out. Limiting him to the food he needs keeps him away from that danger. The limit has nothing to do with moving the food itself.

phrases.english: Rava said:
Since a person is agitated about his property,
if you permit him — he will come to extinguish.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 5
steps.terutzHavaAmina: With no forbidden act, there should be no limit
steps.terutzMaskana: The limit protects against the panicked owner putting out the fire.

steps.title: אביי's challenge from the broken barrel
steps.stepSummary: אביי cites a ברייתא that also limits saving a broken barrel's contents, even though there is no fire there, and asks what decree applies in that case.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: but what about the ברייתא: if a person's barrel broke on top of his roof, he may bring a vessel and place it under it, as long as he does not bring another vessel to catch the liquid, or another vessel to attach. There, what decree is there?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי attacks רבא's reason. In the ברייתא there is a similar limit on saving, but no fire, so the fear of putting out a fire cannot be the explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the same kind of limit appears without any fire, then there must be some other common reason, and that reason could explain the משנה too. אביי's point is that רבא's fire-based reason does not cover the parallel case. התם מאי גזירה איכא is the core of the challenge.

keyTerms.meaning: That which was taught in a ברייתא

phrases.english: Abaye said to him,
but that which was taught in a baraita:
If his barrel broke on top of his roof —
he brings a vessel and places it under it,

phrases.aramaic: וּבִלְבַד שֶׁלֹּא יָבִיא כְּלִי אַחֵר וְיִקְלוֹט,
phrases.english: provided that he does not bring another vessel and catch,
or another vessel and attach.
There, what decree is there?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי, אֶלָּא הָא דְּתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבא's answer
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A parallel limit exists with no fire, so the fire-based decree cannot be the real reason.

steps.title: רבא: the barrel case has its own decree
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that the barrel case has a different decree: the fear that he will carry a vessel through the public domain.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here too it is a decree, lest he bring a vessel through the public domain.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא defends himself. The ברייתא also has a decree, just a different one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the barrel case, the worry is that while rushing to fetch more vessels he will carry one through רשות הרבים, which is forbidden on שבת. So each case has its own protective decree, and רבא's reason for the fire case still stands.

phrases.english: Here too, it is a decree

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁמָּא יָבִיא כְּלִי דֶּרֶךְ רְשׁוּת הָרַבִּים.
phrases.english: lest he bring a vessel through the public domain.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכָא נָמֵי, גְּזֵירָה שֶׁמָּא יָבִיא כְּלִי דֶּרֶךְ רְשׁוּת הָרַבִּים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אביי's challenge
steps.terutzResolutionType: Each case has a separate decree
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The barrel case shows the limit has no fire-related reason
steps.terutzMaskana: The barrel case is limited because of a separate fear of carrying through רשות הרבים.
steps.whatToRemember: Saving from a fire is limited for fear of putting it out. Saving a broken barrel is limited for fear of carrying through רשות הרבים.

steps.title: The גמרא quotes the full barrel ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: Using the word גופא, the גמרא returns to the barrel ברייתא to study it in full, starting with its opening rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: The matter itself: if his barrel broke on top of his roof, he may bring a vessel and place it under it, as long as he does not bring another vessel to catch the liquid, or another vessel to attach.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a closer look at the ברייתא that אביי quoted. It repeats the first part so it can bring the rest.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The repetition is on purpose. Before, the ברייתא was used only as a challenge. Now it is studied for its own content, which continues with more rules. The basic rule stays: one vessel placed directly under the barrel is permitted, but extra vessels are not.

keyTerms.meaning: The matter itself: returning to study a source quoted earlier

phrases.english: The matter itself:
If his barrel broke on top of his roof —
he brings a vessel and places it under it,

phrases.aramaic: וּבִלְבַד שֶׁלֹּא יָבִיא כְּלִי אַחֵר וְיִקְלוֹט,
phrases.english: provided that he does not bring another vessel and catch,
or another vessel and attach.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the ברייתא quoted in step 7 to study it fully
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only one vessel placed directly under the broken barrel is permitted.

steps.title: When guests arrive, extra vessels are allowed
steps.stepSummary: If guests come and he needs more to drink, he may bring extra vessels to catch the liquid and to attach.
steps.simpleTranslation: If guests happened to come to him, he may bring another vessel and catch, and another vessel and attach.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא adds an exception. When there is a real need for the drink on שבת, the extra vessels become permitted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Without guests, the extra saving is only to protect his property, so it is limited. Once guests are present, the drink is needed for שבת itself. That real need allows what was forbidden before.

phrases.english: If guests happened to come to him —
he brings another vessel and catches,
another vessel and attaches.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds an exception to the rule of step 9
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A real שבת need (guests) permits extra vessels.

steps.title: Invite first, then catch
steps.stepSummary: The order matters: he must invite the guests first and only afterward catch the liquid.
steps.simpleTranslation: He should not catch and afterward invite. Rather, he should invite and afterward catch.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא clarifies the order of the exception. The need has to exist before he saves the liquid.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If he catches the liquid before inviting anyone, there was no permitted need at the moment he acted. Only once the guests are already invited does the need permit catching with extra vessels.

phrases.english: And he may not catch and afterward invite,
rather, he invites and afterward catches.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits how the guest exception is applied
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The need (inviting guests) must come before the catching.

steps.title: May one use a trick by inviting guests just to save the wine?
steps.stepSummary: The first view forbids using a trick, meaning inviting guests only in order to save the liquid. רבי יוסי בר יהודה permits even that.
steps.simpleTranslation: And one may not use a trick in this. In the name of רבי יוסי בר יהודה they said: one may use a trick.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא ends with a dispute about הערמה. The question is whether one may invite guests whose real purpose is to save the wine.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first view says the guest exception is only for a real need, not a cover story to save one's property. רבי יוסי בר יהודה allows it, since guests really are present and do drink. This is a classic disagreement about using a permitted method for a hidden purpose.

keyTerms.meaning: Use a clever trick to get around a prohibition
Trickery: doing a permitted act for a hidden purpose

steps.whatToRemember: Saving a broken barrel's contents: one vessel is allowed. Extra vessels are allowed only for a real need such as guests, who must be invited first. The first view forbids using guests as a trick, and רבי יוסי בר יהודה permits it.

phrases.english: And one may not use artifice in this,

phrases.aramaic: מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בַּר יְהוּדָה אָמְרוּ:
phrases.english: in the name of Rabbi Yosei bar Yehuda they said:
one may use artifice.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Concludes the ברייתא with a dispute about trickery
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The first view forbids הערמה. רבי יוסי בר יהודה permits it.

steps.title: Is this the same as an older dispute?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that the barrel dispute about using a trick matches the dispute between רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say that they (the תנא קמא and רבי יוסי בר יהודה) are arguing about the same thing that רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע argued about?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proposes that the argument we just saw about using a trick is really an older, famous argument. This line sets up the next move, which is quoting that older argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 12 showed one opinion forbidding a trick (inviting guests just to save the liquid) and רבי יוסי בר יהודה permitting it. The גמרא now asks whether this is simply a copy of the רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע argument about tricks.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall we say? It introduces a suggestion the גמרא wants to test.

phrases.english: Shall we say that in the dispute
of Rabbi Eliezer and Rabbi Yehoshua they are disagreeing?
phrases.notes: 'They' means the תנא קמא and רבי יוסי בר יהודה from Step 12.

steps.triggerLanguage: לֵימָא בִּפְלוּגְתָּא דְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר וְרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ קָמִיפַּלְגִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries to link the dispute in Step 12 to a known earlier dispute.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is the dispute over using a trick in the barrel case the same as the רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע dispute?

steps.title: The animal and its offspring in a pit
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא: on יום טוב, an animal and its offspring fell into a pit. רבי אליעזר lets you lift only one and feed the other in the pit. רבי יהושע lets you lift both by using a trick.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught: An animal and its offspring fell into a pit (on יום טוב). רבי אליעזר says: You may lift up the first one in order to slaughter it. For the second one, you give it food where it is, so that it does not die. רבי יהושע says: You may lift up the first one in order to slaughter it, and then not slaughter it. Then you use a trick and lift up the second one too. Afterward, he may slaughter whichever one he wants.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the older argument it wants to compare. רבי אליעזר forbids the trick, and רבי יהושע allows it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On יום טוב you may lift an animal out of a pit only to slaughter it for food. A mother and its child may not be slaughtered on the same day (אותו ואת בנו), so only one of them can truly be slaughtered. רבי יהושע allows lifting the first, 'changing your mind' so you can lift the second, and then choosing one to slaughter. That is a trick.

keyTerms.meaning: An animal and its offspring. They may not be slaughtered on the same day.
Food or sustenance, given to the animal while it stays in the pit

steps.confusionAlert: This case is about יום טוב, not שבת. On יום טוב slaughtering for food is allowed, and that is why lifting an animal 'in order to slaughter it' is permitted.

phrases.english: As it was taught:
An animal and its offspring that fell into a pit?
Rabbi Eliezer says:

phrases.aramaic: מַעֲלֶה אֶת הָרִאשׁוֹן עַל מְנָת לְשׁוֹחְטוֹ,
phrases.english: He lifts up the first one in order to slaughter it,
and for the second, he provides it food in its place
so that it does not die.
Rabbi Yehoshua says:

phrases.aramaic: מַעֲלֶה אֶת הָרִאשׁוֹן עַל מְנָת לְשׁוֹחְטוֹ
phrases.english: He lifts up the first one in order to slaughter it
and does not slaughter it,
and he uses a trick and lifts up the second one.
phrases.notes: He claims he changed his mind and now wants to slaughter the second.

phrases.aramaic: רָצָה זֶה שׁוֹחֵט, רָצָה זֶה שׁוֹחֵט.
phrases.english: If he wants, he slaughters this one; if he wants, he slaughters that one.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא: אוֹתוֹ וְאֶת בְּנוֹ שֶׁנָּפְלוּ לְבוֹר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Quotes the source that the suggestion in Step 13 relies on.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי אליעזר forbids the trick and requires feeding the second animal in the pit. רבי יהושע permits the trick and lets you lift both.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר may have had a special reason
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the comparison. רבי אליעזר forbade the trick only because the animal could be fed in the pit. In the barrel case there is no other way to save the liquid.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do you know that? Maybe רבי אליעזר only said this there, because feeding the animal was possible. But here (with the barrel), where there is no other way, he would not forbid it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the comparison. רבי אליעזר's strictness may apply only to the animal case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the pit case there was another solution: feed the animal where it is. So there was no need for a trick. With a leaking barrel nothing can stop the loss, so רבי אליעזר might allow the trick there.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do you know that? It challenges an assumption.
He only said this far, meaning only in that specific case

phrases.english: From what (do you know this)?
Perhaps he only said this far
Rabbi Eliezer, there (in the pit case),
because it is possible to feed it,
but here, where it is not possible, no (he would not forbid it).

steps.triggerLanguage: מִמַּאי? דִּילְמָא עַד כָּאן לָא קָאָמַר רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר הָתָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the comparison from Step 13 by showing a difference on רבי אליעזר's side.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The claim that רבי אליעזר matches the opinion forbidding the trick in the barrel case
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The pit case had another option (feeding), but the barrel case does not.

steps.title: רבי יהושע may have had a special reason
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע may have allowed the trick only because of animal suffering. In the barrel case no animal is suffering.
steps.simpleTranslation: And maybe רבי יהושע only said this there, because there is the issue of animal suffering. But here, where there is no animal suffering, he would not allow it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes its rejection by showing that רבי יהושע's leniency may also apply only to the animal case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An animal stuck in a pit is suffering (צער בעלי חיים), and that is a strong reason to be lenient. Spilled wine does not suffer, so רבי יהושע might forbid the trick there. Since both sides may hold their view only for their own case, the two disputes are not the same.

keyTerms.meaning: There, meaning in the other case

steps.whatToRemember: The barrel dispute is not necessarily the same as the pit dispute. רבי אליעזר may be lenient where there is no other option, and רבי יהושע may be lenient only because of צער בעלי חיים.

phrases.aramaic: וְעַד כָּאן לָא קָאָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ הָתָם,
phrases.english: And Rabbi Yehoshua only said this there,
because there is the suffering of a living creature,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל הָכָא דְּלֵיכָּא צַעַר בַּעֲלֵי חַיִּים — לָא.
phrases.english: but here, where there is no suffering of a living creature, no.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְעַד כָּאן לָא קָאָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ הָתָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the rejection from Step 15 by addressing רבי יהושע.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The claim that רבי יהושע matches רבי יוסי בר יהודה's permission to use a trick
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The pit case involves צער בעלי חיים, but the barrel case does not.

steps.title: Which bread you may save
steps.stepSummary: If you already saved fine bread, you may not then save coarse bread. If you saved coarse bread, you may still save fine bread.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: If someone saved fine bread, he may not then save coarse bread. But if he saved coarse bread, he may then save fine bread.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic: a ברייתא about rescuing bread from a fire on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: You may rescue only what you need for שבת. Once you have good bread, the coarse bread is extra and not needed. If you only have coarse bread, the fine bread is an upgrade you would actually use, so saving it is allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: The Rabbis taught. It introduces a ברייתא.
Fine bread made from sifted flour
Coarse bread made from flour mixed with bran

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
If he saved fine bread,
he may not save coarse bread;
if he saved coarse bread, he may save fine bread.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new ברייתא about rescuing food from a fire.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: You may upgrade from coarse bread to fine bread, but you may not add coarse bread after you already have fine bread.

steps.title: For which day you may save food
steps.stepSummary: You may save food on יום הכפורים for שבת. You may not save food on שבת for יום הכפורים, for יום טוב, or for next שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: You may save food on יום הכפורים for שבת, but not on שבת for יום הכפורים. It goes without saying that you may not save food on שבת for יום טוב, and not on שבת for the next שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: The same ברייתא continues. It explains that you may save food only for the day that comes right after and that truly needs it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If יום הכפורים falls on Friday, the food is needed for the שבת meals that follow, so saving it is allowed. If יום הכפורים falls on Sunday, there is no eating that day, so saving on שבת for it is useless. For יום טוב you can cook on the day itself, and next שבת is too far away, so saving for either of these is plainly not allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: A festival day, when cooking is permitted

phrases.english: And one may save on Yom Kippur for Shabbat,
phrases.notes: When יום הכפורים is on Friday

phrases.english: but not on Shabbat for Yom Kippur.
phrases.notes: There is no eating on יום הכפורים.

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵין צָרִיךְ לוֹמַר מִשַּׁבָּת לְיוֹם טוֹב,
phrases.english: And it goes without saying, not on Shabbat for a Festival,
phrases.notes: You can cook on יום טוב itself.

phrases.english: and not on Shabbat for the next Shabbat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא with a rule about timing.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Food may be saved only for an immediately following day that actually needs it.

steps.title: Bread forgotten in the oven
steps.stepSummary: If bread was left in the oven when שבת began, you may take out enough for three meals and tell others to take some for themselves.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: If someone forgot bread in the oven and שבת began, he may take out enough food for three meals. He may also say to others: Come and take some for yourselves.
steps.whatsHappening: A second ברייתא gives the case of bread left in the oven when שבת started.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This follows the same 'three meals' limit as rescuing food from a fire. It adds that other people may take their own three meals' worth.

keyTerms.meaning: And the day became holy on him, meaning שבת began

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
If he forgot bread in the oven
and the day became sanctified upon him,
one may save food for three meals,
and he says to others:
Come and save for yourselves.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: שָׁכַח פַּת בַּתַּנּוּר וְקִידֵּשׁ עָלָיו הַיּוֹם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a new ברייתא on a related case of saving bread.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Bread left in the oven may be taken out, up to three meals' worth for each person.

steps.title: Take it out with a knife, not a paddle
steps.stepSummary: When removing the bread, he may not use a baker's paddle, only a knife.
steps.simpleTranslation: And when he takes the bread out, he should not use a baker's paddle, but a knife.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא adds that the bread must be removed in an unusual way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The baker's paddle is the normal tool for taking bread out of an oven, so using it looks like a regular weekday activity. A knife is an unusual way to do it.

phrases.english: And when he removes (the bread),
he should not remove it with a baker's paddle,
but with a knife.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a detail about how to remove the bread.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Bread must be removed with a knife, not with a paddle.

steps.title: Removing bread is not a forbidden labor
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the paddle rule. דבי רבי ישמעאל taught that removing bread is a skill and not a מלאכה at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that so? But the school of רבי ישמעאל taught: 'You shall not do any labor.' This excludes blowing the שופר and removing bread from the oven, since these are skills and not labors.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the rule from Step 20. If removing bread is not a מלאכה, why do we need to use a knife?
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to דבי רבי ישמעאל, the Torah does not forbid removing bread at all, because it is a skill (חכמה) and not a מלאכה. So it seems strange to insist on changing the way it is done.

keyTerms.meaning: Is that so? It introduces a challenge.

phrases.english: Is that so?!
But the school of Rabbi Yishmael taught:
'You shall not do any labor,'
this excludes blowing the shofar and removing bread,
which is a skill and not a labor?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִינִי?! וְהָא תָּנָא דְּבֵי רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the requirement from Step 20.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that bread must be removed with a knife and not a paddle
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If removing bread is not a מלאכה at all, there is no reason to require a change in how it is done.

steps.title: Change whatever can be changed
steps.stepSummary: Even though removing bread is permitted, we still change the way we do it whenever we can.
steps.simpleTranslation: As much as it is possible to do it differently, we do it differently.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. Even permitted actions on שבת are done in a changed way when possible.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The knife rule is not because removing bread is forbidden. It is a reminder that today is שבת and not a regular weekday. The rule from Step 20 stands, but its reason is now clearer.

keyTerms.meaning: To change, meaning to do something in an unusual way

steps.whatToRemember: Removing bread from an oven is not a מלאכה. Still, on שבת we do it with a knife, because whatever can be done differently should be done differently.

phrases.english: As much as it is possible to change,
we change.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא in Step 21.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives a new reason for the rule: it is a change made to show the honor of שבת, not because the action is forbidden.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Using a knife must mean that removing bread is a forbidden labor.
steps.terutzMaskana: Removing bread is permitted, but we still change the way it is done whenever possible, to honor שבת.

steps.title: Rise early on Friday to prepare for שבת
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא teaches that a person should get up early on ערב שבת to prepare for שבת. He learns this from the פסוק about the מן on the sixth day.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: A person should always get up early to prepare what he needs for שבת. The פסוק says: 'And it shall be on the sixth day, and they will prepare what they bring.' This means right away.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new teaching about honoring שבת. It is linked to the verses about the מן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק connects collecting the מן on Friday with preparing it. That shows the preparing happened right away, in the morning. So שבת preparations should start early, not at the last minute.

phrases.english: Rav Chisda said:
A person should always rise early
to prepare the needs of Shabbat,
as it says: 'And it shall be on the sixth day'
'and they will prepare what they bring,'
immediately.
phrases.notes: The preparing comes right after the morning collecting.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא: לְעוֹלָם יַשְׁכִּים אָדָם לְהוֹצָאַת שַׁבָּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A side topic about honoring שבת. It leaves the discussion of removing bread from the oven.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A person should rise early on Friday to prepare for שבת, learned from 'והכינו' on the sixth day.

steps.title: Breaking bread over two loaves on שבת
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבא teaches that on שבת you must say המוציא over two loaves, based on the words 'לחם משנה'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבא said: On שבת a person must break bread over two loaves, as it is written: 'double bread.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second teaching learned from the מן: the requirement of two loaves on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On Friday the Jews collected a double portion of מן. That is why we use two whole loaves at the שבת meal to remember it.

keyTerms.meaning: to break / cut the bread (for המוציא)

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for the practice of having two חלות at every שבת meal.

phrases.english: Rabbi Abba said:
On Shabbat a person is obligated to break bread
over two loaves,
as it is written: 'double bread.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אַבָּא: בְּשַׁבָּת חַיָּיב אָדָם לִבְצוֹעַ עַל שְׁתֵּי כִכָּרוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another teaching about שבת learned from the מן verses.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: On שבת one must break bread over two loaves (לחם משנה).

steps.title: רב כהנא held two loaves but cut only one
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי reports that רב כהנא held two loaves and cut only one. He explained that the פסוק says 'collected', not 'broke'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: I saw רב כהנא take two loaves and cut one. He said: 'They collected' is what is written.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains how to carry out רבי אבא's rule. You hold both loaves, but you only need to cut one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says 'לקטו לחם משנה', meaning they gathered a double portion. So the two loaves are needed when you take hold of the bread. Cutting just one loaf is enough.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think you must cut both loaves. The two are needed for holding, and only one is cut.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
I saw Rav Kahana
who took two loaves and cut one.
He said: 'They collected' is what is written.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי: חֲזֵינָא לֵיהּ לְרַב כָּהֲנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how to fulfill the two-loaf rule.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One holds two loaves but needs to cut only one, because the פסוק says 'לקטו'.

steps.title: רבי זירא cut a piece large enough for his whole meal
steps.stepSummary: On שבת, רבי זירא would cut off one piece of bread big enough to last his entire meal.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא would cut a piece large enough for his whole meal.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reports another custom for honoring the שבת bread. This sets up the question that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A large piece shows that he values the שבת bread. It is like showing love for the מצוה of the meal.

phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira would cut a piece
for his entire meal.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי זֵירָא הֲוָה בָּצַע אַכּוּלַּהּ שֵׁירוּתֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another practice for how to break the שבת bread.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי זירא cut one large piece for his whole שבת meal.

steps.title: Doesn't a huge piece look like gluttony?
steps.stepSummary: רבינא asks רב אשי whether cutting such a large piece looks like gluttony.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said to רב אשי: But doesn't that look like gluttony?
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא challenges רבי זירא's practice. Cutting a huge piece of bread might look greedy.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The concern is how it looks to others. Doing a מצוה should not come across as being greedy for food.

phrases.english: Ravina said to Rav Ashi:
But doesn't it look like gluttony?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי זירא's practice.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי זירא's practice of cutting a piece for his whole meal.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A very large piece of bread gives the impression of greed.

steps.title: Not gluttony, because he only does it on שבת
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי answers that he does not do this on other days. Since he does it only on שבת, people see it as honoring שבת, not greed.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Since he does not do this every day, and he does it only now, it does not look like gluttony.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי defends רבי זירא. People can tell the big piece is for שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Gluttony would mean eating this way all the time. A change that happens only on שבת shows it is done to honor the day.

phrases.english: He said to him:
Since every other day he does not do this,
and only now he does it —
it does not look like gluttony.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבינא's challenge.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Context changes how the act is understood.
steps.terutzMaskana: Because it is done only on שבת, it is clearly in honor of שבת.

steps.title: Using the ערוב bread for the שבת blessing
steps.stepSummary: רבי אמי and רבי אסי would say המוציא on the bread of the ערוב. Since one מצוה was already done with it, they wanted to do another מצוה with it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אמי and רבי אסי, when the ערוב bread came to them, would start their meal with it. They said: Since one מצוה was done with it, let another מצוה be done with it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds one more custom about the bread for the שבת meal: using the ערוב bread.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ערוב bread already served a מצוה. Using it for the שבת ברכה adds a second מצוה to the same bread.
steps.whatToRemember: Honoring the שבת bread: two loaves, hold both and cut one, a generous piece, and using ערוב bread so one item serves another מצוה.

phrases.english: Rabbi Ami and Rabbi Asi,
when the eruv bread came to them —
they would begin (the blessing) on it,

phrases.aramaic: אָמְרִי: הוֹאִיל וְאִיתְעֲבִיד בַּהּ חֲדָא מִצְוָה —
phrases.english: they said: Since one מצוה was done with it —
let another מצוה be done with it.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אַמֵּי וְרַבִּי אַסִּי כִּי מִיקְּלַע לְהוּ רִיפְתָּא דְעֵירוּבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: One more practice about the שבת bread, closing the side topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: It is good to use ערוב bread for the שבת ברכה, so another מצוה is done with it.

steps.title: Back to the משנה: how the fire case works
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the משנה's words 'כיצד? נפלה דליקה', which explain how much food may be saved depending on when the fire starts.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'How so? If a fire broke out,' etc.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the משנה. This line sets up the discussion of how many meals a person eats on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says to save food for three meals at night, two in the morning, and one in the afternoon. That assumes there are three שבת meals, so the גמרא now looks at that number.

phrases.english: How so? If a fire broke out, etc.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends the side topic and returns to the משנה about fire.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The amount of food saved depends on when the fire breaks out.

steps.title: How many שבת meals: three or four
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא records a מחלוקת. חכמים say a person must eat three meals on שבת, and רבי חידקא says four.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: How many meals must a person eat on שבת? Three. רבי חידקא says: Four.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא about how many meals are required on שבת. It relates to the משנה's count.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה's three meals match the view of חכמים. רבי חידקא adds a fourth meal. The next step explains the source of each view.

keyTerms.meaning: the תנא who requires four meals

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
How many meals is a person obligated
to eat on Shabbat? Three.
Rabbi Chidka says: Four.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: כַּמָּה סְעוּדוֹת חַיָּיב אָדָם לֶאֱכוֹל בַּשַּׁבָּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא about the number of meals behind the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: חכמים: three שבת meals. רבי חידקא: four.

steps.title: Both views come from the three times 'today' appears in one verse
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says both sides learn from the same פסוק, which says 'היום' three times. רבי חידקא counts those three in addition to the Friday-night meal. חכמים include the night meal in the three.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: Both learned it from one פסוק: 'And משה said: Eat it today, for today is שבת to ה׳, today you will not find it in the field.' רבי חידקא holds these three 'today's are besides the evening meal. The רבנן hold they include the evening meal.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן explains where each side's number comes from. Both use one פסוק, but they count it differently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: משה said this on שבת morning, after the Friday-night meal had already been eaten. רבי חידקא says the three 'today's mean three more meals, making four in total. חכמים say the three include the night meal, making three in total.

keyTerms.meaning: they derived it from one verse

steps.confusionAlert: Both sides agree there are three 'today's. They only disagree about whether the Friday-night meal is one of the three or is added on top.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said,
and both of them derived it from one verse:
'And Moshe said: Eat it today,'
'for today is Shabbat to ה׳,'
'today you will not find it in the field.'
Rabbi Chidka holds:
these three 'today's are besides the evening meal,
and the Rabbis hold: including the evening meal.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן, וּשְׁנֵיהֶם מִקְרָא אֶחָד דָּרְשׁוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source behind each side of the ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The three 'היום' are counted with the night meal (חכמים, three meals) or in addition to it (רבי חידקא, four meals).

steps.title: Quoting the משנה to test רבי חידקא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins quoting the משנה, 'a fire broke out on Friday night', to test רבי חידקא's view of four meals.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned in the משנה: If a fire broke out on Friday night...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a challenge. It quotes the משנה, and the actual question continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה allows saving food for three meals on Friday night. That fits חכמים's count of three meals. The גמרא will ask how this fits רבי חידקא, who says there are four.

phrases.english: We learned in the Mishnah:
If a fire broke out on Friday night
phrases.notes: The quote continues on the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the משנה to test רבי חידקא's opinion.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי חידקא's view of four meals.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה gives a Friday-night fire food for three meals, which matches three meals in total, not four.
